additions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug} returns 403 Forbidden when the requester is not the article owner
additions.reasoning: The specification explicitly states 'any user can update/delete any article' as a security vulnerability (no ownership check on delete). The code raises 403 when the deleting user is not the owner, contradicting the spec.

additions.description: PUT /api/articles/{slug} returns 403 Forbidden when the requester is not the article owner
additions.reasoning: The specification explicitly demonstrates that any user (including non-owners) can update any article, calling it a security vulnerability. The code enforces ownership and raises 403 for non-owners.

additions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/comments/{id} returns 403 when neither the comment author nor the article owner
additions.reasoning: The specification does not describe any ownership restriction on comment deletion; it only tests that the comment author can delete their own comment.

omissions.description: POST /api/profiles/{username}/follow returns 201 but does not return 400 when a user tries to follow themselves
omissions.reasoning: The specification states 'attempt to follow themselves by POST to /api/profiles/follower1/follow. Verify this returns status 400 with message containing cannot be equal'. The code silently does nothing (no follow link created) but returns 200 with no error.

omissions.description: DELETE /api/profiles/{username}/follow does not return 400 when a user tries to unfollow themselves
omissions.reasoning: The specification states 'Verify user1 cannot unfollow themselves (should return 400)'. The code performs no self-unfollow check and returns 200.
The specification states 'Verify the response status is 201' for the follow endpoint. The code uses the default status code of 200.

omissions.description: POST /api/articles/{slug}/comments returns 200 instead of the expected status and returns the full article with comments rather than just the comment
omissions.reasoning: The specification says 'Verify response status is 200' and 'Verify the response article has comments array with length >= 1', which the code satisfies for status. However, the standard RealWorld spec for this endpoint returns {comment: {...}} not {article: {...}}. The spec test checks 'response article has comments array', suggesting the implementation's article-wrapping response is what the spec expects here — this is consistent.

omissions.description: GET /api/articles does not sort by created_at timestamp but by id, which may differ from creation order in edge cases
omissions.reasoning: The specification states 'Verify the articles array is ordered by created timestamp in descending order (newest first)' and references 'ORDER BY article.created DESC'. The code sorts by id instead of created_at.

omissions.description: GET /api/articles/feed does not sort by created_at timestamp but by id
omissions.reasoning: The specification tests feed pagination and ordering. The code sorts feed articles by id rather than created_at, which may not match the expected newest-first ordering by timestamp.

omissions.description: The /api/articles/feed route is registered after /api/articles/{slug}, causing the feed path to be matched as a slug lookup
omissions.reasoning: In FastAPI, routes are matched in registration order. GET /api/articles/feed is registered after GET /api/articles/{slug}, so requests to /api/articles/feed will be handled by get_article with slug='feed' instead of feed_articles. The specification requires a working feed endpoint.
